newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ONE-DAY DEPOS FALL, ZLOTY SLIGHTLY WEAKER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ONE-DAY DEPOS FALL, ZLOTY SLIGHTLY WEAKER.

text.p: Polish one-day deposit rates fell depressed by surpluses on banks' reserve accounts after a recent net inflows from T-bill redemptions boosted the system's liquidity, dealers said.
They said that banks had beefed up reserve accounts this month bracing for bigger outflows in March, due to higher mandatory reserves effective from February 28.

"Market liquidity improved after recent low demand for T-bills and large T-bill redemptions...and banks overbuilt reserves ahead of higher outflows to reserve accounts in March," said Radoslaw Radziszewski from Pekao SA.

At 1000 GMT overnight rates were quoted wide at 13.00/18.00 percent, down from opening's 19.40/20.00 percent and tomorrow/next rates were at 19.00/20.45 percent, down from Tuesday's 20.20/21.60 percent.
The recent low demand for T-bills at primary auctions, which hit a two-year low at around 350 million zlotys was caused by market expectations of a rise in T-bill yields.

The National Bank of Poland is rasing mandatory reserves on zloty call deposits to 20 percent from 17 percent and to four percent from two percent on currency deposits, both on call and term deposits.

The Polish zloty traded slightly weaker against the basket of currencies as the dollar's fall against the mark pushed the zloty lower against the mark but a fear of central bank's dollar-buying intervention prevented the zloty's gain against the U.S. unit, dealers said.

At 1015 GMT the zloty held at 2.95/2.91 percent from the trading band centre, slightly weaker from opening's 3.04/2.95 percent. It was at 3.0365/75 to the dollar, down from 3.0345/69 and at 1.8178/86 to the mark, down from 1.8155/75.
The data on December current account and foreign currency reserves did not have an immediate impact on the market.

Poland's current account deficit was at $368 million in December bringing the shortfall in the whole of 1996 to $1.35 billion while official foreign currency reserves grew by $3.07 billion in 1996 to $18.03 billion.
